task.description:
WF-03 Step 2 -- FIX DESIGN for ISS-0109 (GH#358). Produce a design artefact in lib/letflow/design/ (naming convention: iss0109-<slug>.md, matching lib/letflow/design/iss064-orphaned-tenant-schemas-fix.md). DESIGN ONLY -- no implementation code. ELIXIR-DEV implements it in Step 3.

READ FIRST, in this order: handoffs/WF03-ISS0109-20260821/step-01-issue-fixer-diagnose.json (the diagnosis -- read result.summary in full), then handoffs/WF03-ISS0109-20260821/step-005-issue-fixer-registry-lookup.json, then docs/issues/ISS-0109.yaml. Do not re-derive the diagnosis; it was reached with real evidence and it overturns the issue record's own stated mechanism.

THE DIAGNOSIS IN ONE PARAGRAPH (authoritative for this design; the full evidence is in the Step 1 handoff): ISS-0109's stated mechanism is REFUTED. The logged DROP SCHEMA / DELETE FROM tenant_schemas / DELETE FROM tenants triple is the failing test's OWN post-failure on_exit teardown -- a consequence of the failure, not its cause. schema_name_for_tenant/1 is a pure derivation from the tenant UUID, so the only closure that can name that schema is the one the failing test itself registered; ExUnit runs on_exit callbacks synchronously between tests and kills an over-running runner, so it cannot fire mid-test; and the DROP used IF EXISTS and succeeded, which is what tearing down an already-absent schema looks like. The only line in the original evidence carrying no timestamp is the one asserting causal order. Failure 14 is the more informative of the two and points the same way: promotion_assertion_runs was missing while its schema still existed AND an insert into promotion_reviews in that same schema had already succeeded -- a state DROP SCHEMA ... CASCADE cannot produce. THE FAULT CLASS IS PROVISIONING/REPLAY COMPLETENESS, NOT TEARDOWN TIMING. Candidate (a) (on_exit overlapping the next test) is refuted on ExUnit source; candidate (b) (a concurrent invocation) is a real channel but cannot name that UUID and so is dead as this cause; the reaper is confirmed excluded on fresh evidence (provisioned_at and the reaper cutoff share one clock basis -- measured, not read).

THE SPECIFIC LEAD THE DESIGN MUST RESOLVE: Step 1 identified that provisioned_tenant/0 checks that replay_migrations/1 returned {:ok, _} but never that the resulting schema is actually COMPLETE, and that insert_or_fetch_registration/2 -> re_select_registration/1 (lib/letflow/tenant_provisioning.ex:455-490) returns {:ok, registration} for a PRE-EXISTING tenant_schemas row without guaranteeing the schema it names still exists or that its tables were ever fully created. Both observed failures are consistent with exactly that: failure 3 is a registration accepted for a schema that is absent (3F000), failure 14 is a schema accepted with only some of its tables present (42P01).

YOUR FIRST JOB is to establish, from the code, whether that is a REAL defect in lib/letflow/tenant_provisioning.ex or whether some caller already guarantees the invariant. Say which, with file:line evidence. This determines the shape of everything else:
- If it IS a real defect: the design's primary deliverable is the production-side fix -- what invariant the registration/replay path must guarantee before returning {:ok, _}, and what it must return instead when the invariant does not hold. Note this makes the change a TENANT-DATA-PATH change, so SECURITY-REVIEWER gates it in Step 3; design accordingly (no cross-tenant leakage through a new error value, no new query that is not tenant-scoped).
- If it is NOT a real defect: say so plainly and design only the test-side items below. A design that invents a production change to look substantial is worse than one that reports the production code is already correct.

SCOPE -- IN:
 (C) The completeness invariant above, at whichever layer you establish is correct (production path and/or fixture). Include the post-provision completeness assertion so a partially-migrated tenant schema fails loudly AT the fixture with the state named, rather than 500 lines later as an opaque 42P01.
 (A) A shared test/support helper that provides the tenant fixture used by the two modules ISS-0109 names, and on a provisioning/replay failure captures -- in one shot -- the state that would settle the next occurrence: is the tenant_schemas row present, is the schema present in information_schema.schemata, provisioned_at, the BEAM's utc_now at failure time, and the table list actually present in the schema. This is the artefact that converts the next occurrence from unattributable to attributable.
 (B) Teardown logging distinguishable in the log from a mid-test drop -- the ambiguity that caused the original misdiagnosis. Keep it cheap; this is one identifiable log line, not a logging framework.

SCOPE -- OUT (all already filed; do NOT design fixes for these, and do NOT let the design's rationale depend on them being fixed):
 - ISS-0110/GH#364 -- TenantSchemaReaper's 300s min_age vs a 564-609s suite.
 - ISS-0111/GH#365 -- identity_migration_test's bulk DELETE FROM public.tenant_schemas.
 - ISS-0112/GH#366 -- migrating the other 39 copy-pasted fixture sites onto the new shared helper. THIS RUN ADOPTS THE HELPER IN EXACTLY THE TWO MODULES ISS-0109 NAMES (test/letflow/definitions/promotion_test.exs and test/letflow/definitions/promotion_assertion_rerun_test.exs). Design the helper so the other 39 CAN migrate later, but do not migrate them here.
 - ISS-0113/GH#367 -- Sandbox.mode(:auto) never restored to :manual.
 - ISS-0107/GH#357 -- the nested mix test recursion. Real, and a genuine same-database sharing channel, but not the mechanism behind either ISS-0109 failure.

MANDATORY DESIGN SECTION -- FAIL-FIRST PROVABILITY. WF-03 Step 4 requires a regression test that FAILS against pre-fix code and PASSES against post-fix code. An intermittent, unreproduced failure cannot be regression-tested by waiting for it to recur. So for EVERY behaviour change the design proposes, state concretely how a test can be made to fail against the pre-fix code deterministically -- e.g. by constructing the exact broken state (a tenant_schemas row whose schema was dropped; a schema missing one expected table) and asserting the pre-fix code returns {:ok, _} where the post-fix code must not. If any proposed change CANNOT be shown to fail first, say so explicitly and justify why it still belongs in the design -- do not quietly include it. TEST-DESIGNER will build from this section, so it must be specific enough to build from.

MANDATORY DESIGN SECTION -- WHAT THIS DOES AND DOES NOT CLOSE. State plainly whether shipping this design would make ISS-0109 genuinely FIXED (a root cause removed) or INSTRUMENTED (the next occurrence becomes attributable, cause still unknown). ORCH decides the issue's final status at Step 5 from your answer, so an honest "instrumented, not fixed" is a correct and acceptable outcome -- an overstated one is not, and would put a false 'resolved' into a registry six other issues cross-reference.

CONSTRAINTS:
 - Design artefact only. No implementation code. Interfaces, @specs, state/schema shapes, invariants, failure modes.
 - Do not contradict lib/letflow/design/iss064-orphaned-tenant-schemas-fix.md or any docs/migration/decisions/ record. If the design appears to need to, STOP and flag it for REVIEWER sign-off rather than diverging (core-directives.md).
 - Toolchain note: this host runs Elixir 1.20.3/OTP 29 against a .tool-versions pin of 1.18.3-otp-27 (ISS-0106, already filed, not yours). `mix format --check-formatted` and `mix compile --warnings-as-errors` fail on main itself for that reason. Use plain `mix compile` if you need to check anything.
 - Branch feature/WF03-ISS0109-20260821 is yours. Commit by explicit filename, never `git add -A`.


================================================================================
REWORK ITERATION 1 of 3 -- dispatched by ORCH 2026-08-21T01:51:35Z after CODE-DESIGN-VALIDATOR
returned FAIL on step-02b. Read handoffs/WF03-ISS0109-20260821/step-02b-code-design-validator.json
in full before touching the design.
================================================================================

FIRST, THE PART THAT IS NOT REWORK: the gate CONFIRMED all six load-bearing claims,
independently and at the source. Claim 1 was re-derived from tenant_provisioning.ex
(the CREATE SCHEMA at :188 is at the top level of the transaction fn, and :190 is the
sole call site of insert_or_fetch_registration/2 -- verified by grep across lib/ and
test/). Claim 3 was settled EMPIRICALLY against this workspace's Postgres, not by
argument: after dropping promotion_assertion_runs while leaving version
20260818090001 recorded, a second replay_migrations/1 returned {:ok, []} and the
table was still absent -- so C1 genuinely passes pre-fix and the regression suite is
meaningful. Claim 4's 19-table oracle was re-derived from a fresh schema and is
set-equal to yours. The INSTRUMENTED-not-FIXED verdict was judged honest in BOTH
directions -- the validator specifically checked whether the design secretly removes a
root cause and confirmed it does not. Sections 2, 5, 7 and 8 PASSED this gate. Do not
re-open them, do not "improve" them, and do not restate their conclusions differently.

THE BLOCKING DEFECT -- SS3.2's opts contract, and it is a real one, not a nitpick. An
implementer following SS3.2 literally would write a helper that RAISES on every tenant
insert. Two false statements, both in the same place:

1. SS3.2 declares `status: :disabled | :active | :migrating` in opts. `:disabled` is not
   a legal status. lib/letflow/identity/tenant.ex:56 reads
   `field(:status, Ecto.Enum, values: [:active, :migrating], default: :active)`. The
   validator RAN the insert and got
   `errors: [status: {"is invalid", [... validation: :inclusion, enum: ["active","migrating"]]}]`.

2. SS3.2 says the helper passes opts[:status] to Tenant.create_changeset/3 with
   "default :disabled, matching both current sites". Neither current site passes a
   status at all -- promotion_test.exs:62-72 and promotion_assertion_rerun_test.exs:95-105
   pass only %{slug:, display_name:}. The `:disabled` at those call sites is
   create_changeset/3's THIRD ARGUMENT, the oidc_mode. The design conflated the
   oidc_mode argument with the status field.

Why this blocks rather than being a footnote: SS7.7 and INV-F-5/F-6 commit this design
to behaviour preservation on adoption, and a helper that sets a status where the
current sites set none would move the tenant row off today's default `:active` -- so
the defect contradicts the design's own standard, in addition to not compiling.

SECOND ITEM, same section: disambiguate capture_schema_state/1's failure boundary --
when a per-field capture failure yields `nil` for that field versus when the whole call
returns `{:error, {:capture_failed, _}}`. As written an implementer must guess, and
two implementers would guess differently.

CONSTRAINTS ON THIS REWORK:
- Confine the diff to SS3.2 (plus any cross-reference elsewhere that literally names the
  status/oidc_mode contract and would otherwise contradict the corrected SS3.2 -- grep for
  it rather than assuming there is none).
- Verify the corrected contract against lib/letflow/identity/tenant.ex and the two
  fixture call sites BEFORE writing it. This defect was a reading error about real
  source; do not fix it with another reading of the same kind.
- Still design only. No implementation code.
- Two MINOR observations from the gate, to address in place rather than argue with:
  (a) req022-tenant-schema-provisioning.md:288-294 decides that provision_tenant_schema/1
      never CALLS replay_migrations/2 -- SS2.2 stretches that into "must not VERIFY tables",
      which is a broader claim than the record makes. Narrow SS2.2's wording to what the
      record actually says. The decision to leave production code alone is unaffected and
      stands.
  (b) SS2.2 cites core-directives.md's unoverridable-decision-record clause, but that clause
      is scoped to docs/migration/decisions/ and req022 lives in lib/letflow/design/.
      Cite req022 as the gate-approved design record it is, not as a decision record.
acceptance_criteria: A design artefact exists at lib/letflow/design/iss0109-*.md and contains no implementation code (interfaces, @specs, invariants and failure modes only)

The design states, with file:line evidence, whether insert_or_fetch_registration/2 -> re_select_registration/1 returning {:ok, registration} without guaranteeing the named schema exists and is fully migrated is a REAL defect in lib/letflow/tenant_provisioning.ex or is already guaranteed by a caller

The design covers scope items (A) shared test/support fixture helper with one-shot failure-state capture, (B) teardown logging distinguishable from a mid-test drop, and (C) the post-provision completeness invariant -- or explicitly justifies dropping any of them
The design explicitly limits helper adoption to the two modules ISS-0109 names, and does not design a migration of the other 39 copy-paste sites (ISS-0112)
A FAIL-FIRST PROVABILITY section states, per proposed behaviour change, how a test can be made to fail deterministically against pre-fix code -- specific enough for TEST-DESIGNER to build from
A WHAT THIS DOES AND DOES NOT CLOSE section states plainly whether this makes ISS-0109 FIXED (root cause removed) or INSTRUMENTED (next occurrence attributable, cause still unknown)
The design does not propose fixes for ISS-0110, ISS-0111, ISS-0112, ISS-0113 or ISS-0107, and its rationale does not depend on any of them being fixed
No contradiction with lib/letflow/design/iss064-orphaned-tenant-schemas-fix.md or any docs/migration/decisions/ record (or the contradiction is flagged for REVIEWER rather than resolved unilaterally)

result.summary:
WF-03 Step 2 fix design for ISS-0109 (GH#358) complete. Artefact: lib/letflow/design/iss0109-provisioning-completeness-and-fixture-instrumentation.md (631 lines, 11 sections). Design only -- no implementation code, no function bodies, no .ex/.exs source blocks; the one fenced block is an @spec/@type contract listing.

=== FIRST JOB: IS insert_or_fetch_registration/2 -> re_select_registration/1 A REAL PRODUCTION DEFECT? ===
VERDICT: NO -- and no production change is proposed. The lead has two halves and they resolve differently (design section 2):
(a) 'returns {:ok, registration} without guaranteeing the named schema exists' -- REFUTED ON CODE. provision_tenant_schema/1 (lib/letflow/tenant_provisioning.ex:164) opens one Repo.transaction/1 at :170 and, INSIDE it, runs pg_advisory_xact_lock at :174, then CREATE SCHEMA IF NOT EXISTS "<schema>" UNCONDITIONALLY at :188 -- on every call, including the idempotent second one -- and only THEN reaches insert_or_fetch_registration/2 at :190, whose re_select_registration/1 branch (:483-:488, entered from :471) is the pre-existing-row path. So that branch never skips schema creation: DDL is transactional, and at the moment {:ok, %Registration{}} is returned the named schema exists. The diagnosis's own wording ('without re-creating anything INSIDE the schema') is exact; 'inside' is the operative word. The 'row could name a different schema' variant is closed too: Registration.changeset/2 (lib/letflow/tenant_provisioning/registration.ex:57-65) validate_format's ^tenant_[0-9a-f]{32}$ (ISS-0027/GH#85) plus two DB-backed unique_constraints, schema_name_for_tenant/1 (:101-:106) is pure/total/injective, and lib/ contains no changeset-bypassing writer (the only other from(r in Registration, ...) in lib/ is mark_migrations_applied/1 at :497-:502, an update_all of one column). Logged as OQ-2, not as a defect.
(b) '...or that its tables were ever fully created' -- TRUE, but it is a DECIDED DESIGN INVARIANT, not a defect. Table creation is replay_migrations/2 (:238-:264), a separate primitive; the separation is stated at tenant_provisioning.ex:18-23 ('two separate, composable primitives -- neither calls the other') and, gate-approved, at lib/letflow/design/req022-tenant-schema-provisioning.md:288-294 as the 'No implicit chaining invariant', and is enforced by replay_migrations/2 returning {:error, :tenant_not_provisioned} rather than provisioning on the fly. Making provision_tenant_schema/1 guarantee table completeness would CONTRADICT that record, so per core-directives.md's Instruction Precedence this design declines it rather than resolving it unilaterally. The completeness obligation belongs to whoever SEQUENCES the two primitives -- in both ISS-0109 failures that is the test fixture (promotion_test.exs:78-98, asserting only {:ok, _} from replay at :96; promotion_assertion_rerun_test.exs:112-133, replay assert at :130). THAT is the real gap, and it is at the fixture layer.
CONSEQUENCE: lib/letflow/tenant_provisioning.ex and .../registration.ex are NOT modified. This is therefore NOT a tenant-data-path change -- nothing touches an API route, migration, response shape or secret -- so SECURITY-REVIEWER's trigger is not armed; INV-F-8/INV-F-9 keep it that way (every helper query is single-tenant-scoped or a catalog read filtered by table_schema = $1; the only identifier interpolation reuses schema_name_for_tenant/1's output, the same INV-7 argument tenant_provisioning.ex:180-187 already makes).

=== WHAT SCOPE ITEMS A/B/C BECAME ===
All three are IN, and all land in test/ only. New test-only module Letflow.TenantFixture (test/support/tenant_fixture.ex), a plain module beside Letflow.TenantSchemaReaper -- not a GenServer, never supervised, never referenced from lib/. Four public functions with full @spec/@type contracts in design section 3.2: provisioned_tenant!/1 -> tenant_fixture(); capture_schema_state/1 -> {:ok, schema_state()} | {:error, {:capture_failed, Exception.t()}}; assert_schema_complete!/2 -> :ok (raises); expected_tenant_tables/0 -> [String.t()].
(A) SHARED HELPER + ONE-SHOT CAPTURE (section 3.5): a 14-field schema_state() gathered in a single call at the moment of failure -- registration_present?, provisioned_at, migrations_applied_at, schema_present? (information_schema.schemata), tables_present/tables_missing (information_schema.tables), applied_versions/manifest_versions/versions_missing ("<schema>".schema_migrations vs tenant_scoped_migrations/0 at :430-:431), observed_at_utc, db_now (SELECT now() at time zone 'utc'), pg_backend_pid. Every field is mapped in a table to the specific question the ISS-0109 diagnosis could not answer. Contract: never raises to its caller (mirrors sweep_orphans/2's contract at test/support/tenant_schema_reaper.ex:50-56), best-effort per field, no retry/poll (a retry observes a different state than the one that failed), emitted twice -- into the ExUnit.AssertionError message and via Logger.error carrying the section-3.6 marker.
(B) TEARDOWN LOGGING (section 3.6): exactly ONE log line before the DROP, carrying the fixed literal marker LETFLOW_TENANT_FIXTURE plus a CLOSED phase vocabulary -- teardown | provision_failed | replay_failed | incomplete_schema -- plus schema name, tenant id, schema_present_before_drop, and the owning test module/name. The teardown path may emit only phase=teardown and the failure paths only the other three, so a phase=teardown line is by construction never a mid-test drop. Today's three teardown statements are unchanged in content and order (INV-F-5). One line, :info level, no new dependency, no config change.
(C) COMPLETENESS INVARIANT (sections 3.3/3.4), placed at the FIXTURE layer per the section-2 verdict: assert_schema_complete!/2 asserts three things -- schema present in information_schema.schemata; tables_missing == [] against a 19-table oracle; versions_missing == [] against the manifest. Check 3 catches 'replay never fully ran'; check 2 catches failure 14's exact state (a recorded version whose table is nonetheless absent), which check 3 alone cannot see -- both are required. The oracle is the 19 tables derived from the manifest's 31 entries (events, instance_sequence, instance_projections, event_payload_store, events_archive, event_idempotency, event_type_registry, process_definitions, instance_definition_snapshots, promotion_reviews, promotion_assertion_runs, tokens, tasks, groups, tenant_role, users, lua_script_execution_audit, instance_state_snapshots, variable_schemas), hard-coded ONLY because a MANDATORY oracle-rot guard test (set equality in both directions against a freshly provisioned schema, mirroring REQ-082/ISS-0037's service-existence-oracle obligation) fails loudly the day a 32nd manifest entry lands. Without that guard the list must not be hard-coded (INV-F-7).

=== ADOPTION BOUNDARY (section 5) ===
EXACTLY the two modules ISS-0109 names: promotion_test.exs (replaces insert_tenant!/0 :62, drop_schema!/1 :74, provisioned_tenant/0 :78-98; its 8 call sites keep their %{tenant_id:, schema_name:} destructuring) and promotion_assertion_rerun_test.exs (:95, :112-133; 11 call sites) -- but its drop_schema!/1 at :107 STAYS, because :463 has a second, unrelated caller for a SandboxPool-held schema. The other 39 sites are explicitly NOT migrated (ISS-0112/GH#366); the helper is shaped so all per-site variation rides in opts so they CAN migrate later. Letflow.DataCase is not modified.

=== FAIL-FIRST PROVABILITY PLAN, IN BRIEF (section 7) ===
No test waits for a recurrence (Step 1's stressor produced 828/828 passes). Every change fails first by CONSTRUCTING the broken state, using provisioned_tenant!(teardown: false) so the fixture's own teardown cannot repair or race the construction. C1 missing TABLE: provision normally, then DROP TABLE "<schema>"."promotion_assertion_runs" leaving the schema and every schema_migrations row intact = failure 14's exact state; pre-fix the fixture still returns success (the version is recorded, so Migrator re-applies nothing) and the failure surfaces later as 42P01, post-fix it raises with tables_missing == ["promotion_assertion_runs"]. C2 missing SCHEMA: DROP SCHEMA CASCADE leaving the tenant_schemas row = failure 3's state; post-fix raises with schema_present? == false, and after a re-provision (which re-creates an EMPTY schema per :188) with all 19 tables missing -- explicitly flagged that this proves FIXTURE detection, not a production behaviour change, and that any assertion on pre-fix {:ok, %Registration{}} here is a CHARACTERIZATION test, not the regression assertion. C3 missing VERSION: delete the highest schema_migrations row and its table; both versions_missing and tables_missing non-empty. C4 capture fidelity across all four states, plus a negative test that a wholly absent tenant yields {:ok, state} with both present? flags false and does NOT raise (INV-F-4); db_now vs observed_at_utc asserted within a BOUND, to catch a clock-BASIS error (the UTC-vs-local skew that cost Step 1 a five-hour reconciliation), not jitter. C5 log distinguishability under ExUnit.CaptureLog. C6 the oracle-rot guard. C1-C6 are all deterministic; C4-C6 also fail first trivially because the functions do not exist pre-fix.
ONE ITEM WITH NO FAIL-FIRST PROOF, DECLARED (section 7.7): the two modules' ADOPTION of the helper. It is a refactor with no behaviour delta by construction (INV-F-5/INV-F-6), so no pre-fix state distinguishes it. It stays in because without it none of C1-C6 protects the two sites ISS-0109 actually names. Its evidence standard is behaviour-preservation instead -- both modules pass in full pre- and post-adoption, with TEST-RUNNER quoting both runs -- and the design states plainly that this is weaker than fail-first rather than dressing it up.

=== FIXED vs INSTRUMENTED VERDICT (section 8) ===
INSTRUMENTED, NOT FIXED. Genuinely fixed: a real fixture-layer gap (a partially-migrated schema now fails AT the fixture naming the missing tables instead of ~500 lines later as an opaque 42P01, with deterministic fail-first proof), the misdiagnosis class (the phase= vocabulary makes a teardown structurally impossible to mistake for a mid-test drop), and attributability of the next occurrence. NOT fixed: the root cause remains UNKNOWN -- no production defect was found so there is no production cause to remove, the failure was never reproduced, and the live sharing channels (ISS-0110's 300s reaper window, ISS-0107's nested invocation, ISS-0111's bulk registry delete) are all still open and out of scope. If any of them is the real cause this design does not stop it; it only ensures the next occurrence says so. RECOMMENDATION to ORCH for Step 5: do NOT close ISS-0109 as resolved -- keep it open (or an 'instrumented'/'monitoring' state if the registry has one), correct its mechanism: section per Step 1's MAJOR finding, and extend related: with ISS-0107 and ISS-0059. ORCH owns the final call; this is the input to it.

=== SCOPE-OUT AND NON-CONTRADICTION ===
No fix is proposed for ISS-0110/0111/0112/0113/0107, and no invariant or rationale depends on any of them being fixed (section 1.2 states why each is excluded; section 9 lists 8 things ELIXIR-DEV must not change, including the reaper, test_helper.exs, DataCase, the 39 other sites, and restoring Sandbox.mode(:manual) anywhere). ISS-0113 is deliberately NOT absorbed: the helper reproduces today's Sandbox.mode(:auto)-without-restore behaviour exactly (INV-F-6). Non-contradiction check against iss064-orphaned-tenant-schemas-fix.md and docs/migration/decisions/ is in section 6: nothing alters the reaper, test_helper.exs, sweep_orphans/2's contract or its min_age default, and the schema-name regex is not re-duplicated. The ONE place a contradiction was available -- req022's No-implicit-chaining invariant -- is DECLINED rather than resolved, so no REVIEWER escalation is required by this design.

Four open questions are stated explicitly rather than guessed (section 10): OQ-1 where the incomplete schema comes from (unresolved, deliberately -- it is the question the capture exists to answer); OQ-2 the changeset validates schema_name's shape but not equality with the derivation (unreachable today, observation only); OQ-3 whether the oracle should be derived rather than hard-coded; OQ-4 the effective test Logger level -- if :info is filtered in CI the teardown line disappears and scope item (B) is defeated, so ELIXIR-DEV must confirm it and raise that one line to :warning rather than reconfiguring the logger globally.

Toolchain note: no mix command was run for this step -- it is a design artefact with no compilable output, and per the handoff this host's Elixir 1.20.3/OTP 29 against the 1.18.3-otp-27 pin (ISS-0106) already fails mix format --check-formatted and mix compile --warnings-as-errors on main itself. Nothing under lib/letflow/*.ex, priv/ or test/ was modified by this step; the only files changed are the design artefact and this handoff.

=== REWORK ITERATION 1 (2026-08-21T01:53:54Z) -- SS3.2 opts contract corrected, SS3.5 failure boundary disambiguated, two MINOR wording narrowings in SS2.2 ===

VERIFIED AT SOURCE FIRST, BEFORE WRITING (the gate's instruction, since the original defect was a reading error):
 - lib/letflow/identity/tenant.ex:56 -- field(:status, Ecto.Enum, values: [:active, :migrating], default: :active). Read directly. `:disabled` is NOT in the enum.
 - lib/letflow/identity/tenant.ex:76-79 -- @spec create_changeset(t, attrs, oidc_mode :: :enabled | :disabled) and def create_changeset(tenant, attrs, oidc_mode) when oidc_mode in [:enabled, :disabled]. The THIRD positional argument is the oidc_mode.
 - promotion_test.exs:62-72 and promotion_assertion_rerun_test.exs:95-105 -- read both call sites in full. Each passes attrs = %{slug: TenantSlugFixture.unique_slug(...), display_name: "..."} and the bare atom `:disabled` as the third argument. NEITHER passes :status. Both therefore land on the schema default :active.
 - create_changeset/3 casts [:slug, :display_name, :status, :idp_realm_id], so :status IS castable -- it is simply never set by either current site.

WHAT CHANGED IN SS3.2 (the corrected contract, quoted):
 1. opts type -- the `status:` key is REMOVED and replaced by the real third argument:
      @type opts :: [
              slug_prefix: String.t(),
              display_name: String.t(),
              oidc_mode: :enabled | :disabled,
              expected_tables: [String.t()] | :default,
              teardown: boolean()
            ]
 2. Step 2 rewritten. It now reads, normatively: 'Insert a Letflow.Identity.Tenant via Tenant.create_changeset/3, called with **exactly two cast attributes** -- slug: from Letflow.TenantSlugFixture.unique_slug(opts[:slug_prefix]) and display_name: from opts[:display_name] -- and with opts[:oidc_mode] as the **third positional argument**, defaulting to :disabled.' It then carries the three source citations above as an explicit evidence list, including that ':disabled is not a member of that enum; casting it produces an invalid changeset (validation: :inclusion), so a helper that passed it would raise on every insert.'
 3. The status question is closed rather than left open: 'Consequently opts carries **no :status key**. Omitting the field is what preserves today's behaviour: both adopted sites currently get the schema default :active (INV-F-5).' A future ISS-0112 adopter needing a non-default status may add the key then, constrained to :active | :migrating, and it MUST NOT be added speculatively here.
 This resolves BOTH halves of the gate's MAJOR: the illegal enum value is gone, and the design no longer moves the tenant row off :active, so it no longer contradicts its own SS7.7 / INV-F-5 / INV-F-6 behaviour-preservation standard.
 4. Also in SS3.2 (the gate's 5th MINOR, same section): step 7's claim that all call sites destructure %{tenant_id:, schema_name:} is corrected -- promotion_test.exs:464-465 binds %{tenant_id:} alone. CAPTURE_SCHEMA_STATE/1 FAILURE BOUNDARY (SS3.5) -- resolved as NESTED rules, not competing ones, and stated as normative rather than left to the implementer:
 - Every field is gathered inside its OWN guard. A single failing query is ALWAYS a per-field degradation -- nil for scalars, [] for lists -- and the call still returns {:ok, schema_state()} with every other field populated. Never a whole-call failure.
 - Derived fields follow their inputs: if tables_present degraded to [], tables_missing is [] too -- NOT 'all 19 missing' -- because an unobserved set must never be reported as an observed absence. Same for applied_versions/versions_missing. (This was implicit before and is the one place an implementer could have produced a misleading report.)
 - {:error, {:capture_failed, exception}} is the OUTER safety net only: a failure outside the per-field guards (assembling the result map raises, or tenant_id is malformed so no field can be attempted). Explicitly NOT reachable by any single field's query failing.
 - An absent tenant or absent schema is NOT a capture failure -- {:ok, state} with the present? flags false (INV-F-4).

 Neither narrowing changes the outcome: production code (lib/letflow/tenant_provisioning.ex, .../registration.ex) is still NOT modified, so this remains a test-only change and SECURITY-REVIEWER's tenant-data-path trigger is still not armed.
